authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2757 kaphoṇi gives Hindi kohni/kehunī, Bengali kanui and Western Pahari khunni “elbow”. Simple contracted q/k and vowel variants preserve this historical elbow family. Reviewed comparison: Kathoriya kihuni “elbow” (f_7mcommfhbbnng). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 135.1 aṅguli explicitly gives Maithili ā̃gur, Nepali aũlo and Lahnda aṅgal “finger”. The Maiya agui-type form is separately listed under 135.2 *aṅgūḍi and is assigned there; opaque reduced or retroflex-r forms remain distinct audit questions. Reviewed comparison: Dang ʌ̃ŋɡʌɾi “finger” (f_7ioamkt7uje7c). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10234 mūtra explicitly gives Kalasha mūtra, Bshk. mūλ and Western Pahari mūc. The survey lateral/sibilant outcomes fit the tr-cluster urine family; retroflex muṭ and ordinary mute preserve the same noun, with phonetic details left open. Reviewed comparison: Buksa mut “urine” (f_fgdpypslzzy6u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12598 śṛṇoti explicitly gives Bhojpuri sunal and western suṇṇo “hear”. Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology. Reviewed comparison: Buksa suna “he hears; he heard” (f_zzsmb6m2x457u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
